claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 18 and still lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, studying for A-levels, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, that would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to fully assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you at home, or do you provide financial support for him (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money) that's at least equal to the Child Benefit amount?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about the benefits - I don't know if he's receiving any benefits in his own right like Universal Credit or ESA. He's not working 24 hours a week though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me, I can make an assessment:

Since Alex is:
- 18 years old (under 20)
- In approved education (studying for A-levels at sixth form college)
- Living with you in the UK
- Not working 24 hours or more per week
- Not being claimed for by anyone else

You would generally be eligible for Child Benefit for him, **provided he is not receiving certain benefits in his own right** such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

However, since you're unsure whether Alex is receiving any benefits in his own right, I cannot make a completely definitive determination. If Alex is claiming benefits like Universal Credit or ESA independently, this would disqualify him from Child Benefit.

**Would you be able to check whether Alex is receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?** This is important information to confirm your eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. I'll need to check with Alex about whether he's claiming any benefits himself. Is there anything else I need to know about the eligibility requirements, or should I come back once I've confirmed that information?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You've provided most of the key information I need. The main outstanding question is whether Alex is receiving benefits in his own right, which you'll need to confirm with him.

Once you've checked that with Alex, please do come back and let me know. If he's not receiving any benefits in his own right, then based on everything you've told me, you should be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

Just to summarize what would make you eligible:
- Alex is under 20 and in approved education (A-levels) ✓
- He lives with you in the UK ✓
- No one else is claiming for him ✓
- He's not working 24+ hours per week ✓
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right (needs confirmation)

Is there anything else you'd like to ask me about Child Benefit eligibility before you check that information?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I think that's clear. Thank you for your help - I'll check with Alex about the benefits and get back to you if needed.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Yes, please do check with Alex about whether he's receiving any benefits in his own right, and feel free to come back once you have that information so I can give you a definitive answer on your eligibility.

Best of luck, and I'm here if you need any further assistance!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much for your time and help. I appreciate it!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions after speaking with Alex.

Have a great day!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thanks, you too! Bye!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Goodbye! All the best!
